title: Alas and Did My Savior Bleed
lyrics_original: Alas, and did my Savior bleed
And did my Sovereign die?
Would He devote that sacred Head
For such a worm as I?
Was it for crimes that I had done
He groaned upon the tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!
Well might the sun in darkness hide
And shut his glories in,
When Christ, the Mighty Maker died,
For man the creature’s sin.
Thus might I hide my blushing face
While His dear Cross appears,
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt my eyes to tears.
But drops of grief can ne’er repay
The debt of love I owe:
Here, Lord, I give myself away,
‘Tis all that I can do.

bible_verses.english: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
But he was wounded for our transgressions. He was bruised for our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace was on him; and with his stripes we are healed.
who himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness; by whose stripes you were healed.

devotional.prayer_english: Lord Jesus, I am filled with wonder when I think of Your sacrifice on the cross for me. You bore my grief, carried my sins, and showed a love far beyond my comprehension. Thank You for Your incredible grace that paid my debt and brought me peace. Help me to live every day in the light of Your love, offering my heart back to You in gratitude. Amen.

devotional.reflection_english: Isaac Watts’ classic hymn gently stops us in our tracks, asking us to ponder the sheer weight and wonder of the cross. It is astonishing to realize that the King of Glory chose to lay down His life for our sins, pouring out an unimaginable love that we could never earn. When we look at His sacrifice, our hearts are moved from quiet grief to profound gratitude. As you sing today, let His endless grace wash over you and invite your heart into deeper surrender.
